analyses.failure: test_chk_019_apb5_user_signals [apb5.s1, user.s1]: CHK-033/031 o_apb_pslverr in PREADY cycle expected 0x1, got 0x0
analyses.spec_says: spec/AsyncAPBBridge_Design_Specification.md:130 REQ-FUNC-002 "The bridge shall return on the requester-side interface the response of the completer-side transfer unchanged: PRDATA of a read, PSLVERR, ..."; :134 REQ-FUNC-006 "PSLVERR on the requester-side interface shall be high only in the PREADY cycle, and only when the completer-side PSLVERR was high at the end of the completer-side transfer" (rules.json:678-683, AB2-3-11); :247 o_apb_pslverr "Loaded with o_apb_pready, cleared at the next edge"; :531 ERR-001 "Forwarded: o_apb_pslverr high in the o_apb_pready cycle". contract.json:985-987 CHK-033: "In each requester PREADY cycle, o_apb_pslverr equals i_apb_pslverr sampled at C".
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_mst.sv:244 `assign o_apb_pslverr = 1'b0;` — the output is tied to constant 0. The slv side does pack PSLVERR (m_vlsit_apbcdc_slv.sv:144 `w_resp_payload[PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W] = i_apb_pslverr`), and the mst loads it into reg_resp_payload[DATA_W] at the PREADY edge (mst.sv:233-234) and clears it in RESP (mst.sv:235-236), but that bit is never connected to the port. Comment at mst.sv:240-241 says outputs are "sliced from the response output registers ... PRDATA, PSLVERR, ...", so the tie-off disagrees with the block's own comment. So in the PREADY cycle o_apb_pslverr=0 whatever the completer drove.
analyses.test_does: The CHK-019 policy (test_async_apb_bridge.py:787-794) sets pslverr=r.randint(0,1), so about half the transfers complete with i_apb_pslverr=1. The Completer drives it with pready=1 (:694-696). At completion edge C the response is captured into rec.resp (:558-562). Requester._complete (:459-461) compares out['pslverr'] with exp_resp (:256) `pslverr = rs['pslverr'] & 1`, which is the value sampled at C. So expected=1, observed=0.

candidates.evidence_for: mst.sv:244 hard-wires o_apb_pslverr to 0 even though the response register holds the PSLVERR bit (mst.sv:233-236) and the slv packs it (slv.sv:144). This contradicts REQ-FUNC-002/006 (spec:130,134), the port table (spec:247) and ERR-001 (spec:531). Every config and every test where the completer drives pslverr=1 fails in the same way; test_chk_031, whose policy uses err_p=0.0 (:1147), passes in apb4.s1.log:582.
candidates.evidence_against: None found. The assignment cannot be justified as a configuration option: the spec says PSLVERR is 'always present' (spec:123).

candidates.evidence_for: The test expectation is derived from the completer value sampled at C (:558-562, :256), which matches the spec. No test issue found.
candidates.evidence_against: The expected value follows CHK-033's 'o_apb_pslverr equals i_apb_pslverr sampled at C' (contract.json:987) exactly. The sampling of the completer inputs at C is correct, because prdata in the same transfer is checked against the same snapshot and does not fail.

candidates.evidence_for: None — the spec is consistent across REQ-FUNC-002, REQ-FUNC-006, the port table, ERR-001 and OP-004 (spec:424).
candidates.evidence_against: Several clauses state without ambiguity that PSLVERR is forwarded with PREADY.
